docs.dcterms_abstract:
He hears the expedition against the Mahrattas turned out unfortunate.
Mr. Bellas' promotion thereby strongly censured in England and disapproved
by the Ministry. The Company and the Government at loggerheads,
the latter refusing to renew their contract for more than 10
years. He reports events of last year - fleets of France and Spain
were days in the Channel off Plymouth, vigorous measures taken for
its defence, large body of tinmen from Cornwall brought into the
town; enemy fleet threatened for some days but then retired; great
ferment, all over the nation; the "Patriots" have called meeting and
drawn up petitions to Parliament; associations and committees formed
to act in concert with the chief aim of distressing the Government;
warm work in the H. of C.; Ld. Shelburne and C. Fox surrounded(?)
Sir George Rodney defeated the Spanish Fleet and blockaded Gibralta.
We have recovered Georgia and have good news from the Spanish Indies.
He proceeds to various items of family news, e.g., promising care
about the pictures - "the gentoo image occupies a niche in my new
library".

docs.dcterms_abstract:

a later paragraph he informs her that Mr. Mauritius Lowe, a close
relative of your late Lord, had by his recommendation received an
allowance of £10, which was due on July 26th and ventures to hope
Your Ladyship, of her charity, will continue his late Lordship's
benefaction.

docs.dcterms_abstract:
Mostly illegible. He is glad to hear that the children are settled
to your satisfaction at Dorchester. He also writes to Mr. Bowman to
ask for an account of Mrs. Bellas' expenses on the road to London
from their landing from the ship at Deal; and whether Capt. Cornwalls
has paid his share for self and servant. Mr. Bowman replies
that he has not had any settlement with Capt. Cornwallis, as he has
written to Mrs. Bellas to say he will endeavour if he can to collect
the road bills of expenses. These expenses are set out item by item
in f.298, amounting to £18 9s. 6d. leaving credit balance of
£2 10s. 6d. (Expenses at Deal, Canterbury, Sittingbourne, Dartford,
respectively on hire of chaises and ostler boys).

docs.dcterms_abstract:
An intimate letter in which he tells Mrs. N. to expect his Mary Ann
and her brother by the Maidstone coach on Friday evening, who he
says are most eager to come and stay and spend their holidays. He
alludes affectionately to his children, one of whom is interrupting
him as he writes. He congratuates them that the Jacobins round them
have fallen. The things ordered at his warehouse have gone and he
has asked his son to enquire about those ordered for Mr. Swaine.
f.97 notifies that the 2 casks sent by Mr. Swaine are at Whately's
warehouse in Maidstone.
